name: Vermont

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Vermont became the 14th state on March 4, 1791.

events.title: 1800 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1800 census, Vermont's House delegation grew from 2 to 4 seats.

events.title: 1810 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1810 census, Vermont's House delegation grew from 4 to 6 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 13th through 16th Congresses (1813–1821), Vermont elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1820 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1820 census, Vermont's House delegation shrank from 6 to 5 seats.

events.title: 1830 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1830 census, Vermont kept 5 seats in the House.

events.title: 1840 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1840 census, Vermont's House delegation shrank from 5 to 4 seats.

events.title: 1850 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1850 census, Vermont's House delegation shrank from 4 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1860 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1860 census, Vermont kept 3 seats in the House.

events.title: 1870 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1870 census, Vermont kept 3 seats in the House.

events.title: 1880 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1880 census, Vermont's House delegation shrank from 3 to 2 seats.

events.title: 1890 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1890 census, Vermont kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1900 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1900 census, Vermont kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1910 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1910 census, Vermont kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Vermont's House delegation shrank from 2 to 1 seat. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Vermont kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c007.text: Vermont's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1800 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c008.text: New map drawn after the 1800 census, which raised Vermont's seats from 2 to 4. It was first used in the 1802 election.

c013.text: After the 1810 census changed Vermont's seats from 4 to 6, Vermont still elected all of its members statewide, so it had no districts to redraw.

c017.text: Vermont's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1820 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c018.text: New map drawn after the 1820 census, which cut Vermont's seats from 6 to 5. It was first used in the 1822 election.

c019.text: Vermont's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1824 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c022.text: Vermont's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1830 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c023.text: New map drawn after the 1830 census, which left Vermont with 5 seats. It was first used in the 1832 election.

c028.text: New map drawn after the 1840 census, which cut Vermont's seats from 5 to 4. It was first used in the 1842 election.

c033.text: New map drawn after the 1850 census, which cut Vermont's seats from 4 to 3. It was first used in the 1852 election.

c048.text: New map drawn after the 1880 census, which cut Vermont's seats from 3 to 2. It was first used in the 1882 election.

c073.text: New map drawn after the 1930 census, which cut Vermont's seats from 2 to 1. It was first used in the 1932 election.
